fields.meta_title: Funny Survey Questions With Examples | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Funny survey questions with examples for coworkers, families, and students, and four surveys that put the answers to use.
fields.h1: Build Funny Survey Questions Whose Answers Get Used
fields.hero_description: Get funny survey questions in a survey built from a prompt, with every answer saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Survey Does With the Jokes
fields.features_subheading: Six things the survey handles after the funny questions are written, including who gets a vote and where the results go.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted for your crowd

Describe who is answering and how far the jokes can go. Emergent drafts the questions and their answer choices, and you swap out any one of them with a follow-up prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Votes counted by name

Ask people to vote for a teammate or a relative from a list of names. The survey tallies the votes for each name, then shows the leader and the runner-up when voting closes.
fields.feature_3:
One question per screen

Run the survey as a conversation, one question at a time. Each punchline gets its own screen on a phone and nobody has to scroll past a joke to reach the next answer box.
fields.feature_4:
Answers in a database you own

Each answer is saved with the person's team or class in a database you own. Filter by team to see which department voted for the toaster, then reuse the list next quarter.
fields.feature_5:
Results sent to Slack or email

Send the tally to a Slack channel or an inbox when the survey closes. A reminder goes out the day before to anyone who has not answered yet, and nobody else gets nudged.
fields.feature_6:
No cap on answers

Emergent puts no cap on survey responses, and a company of 900 people can all vote. Host it on your own domain, paid in credits, and export the code to GitHub on paid plans.

fields.usecase_heading: What Four Funny Surveys Were For
fields.tab_content_1:
Six silly answers sort the offsite into teams

Before the offsite, all 40 people answer silly multiple choice questions, like which office appliance they would be. The survey sorts them into 5 teams of 8, with no more than 2 people from any department on a team. Team Toaster ends up with people from 4 departments.
fields.tab_content_2:
The reunion awards, voted before anyone arrives

Before the family reunion, 23 relatives get a link to vote by name on joke awards, such as longest dinner story. Each award gets its own screen and a list of names to pick from. Dana takes longest dinner story with 9 of 23 votes, and every winner goes onto the award list printed for Saturday.
fields.tab_content_3:
A class mascot picked before the bell

When term starts, 27 students answer funny questions on their phones, a question per screen, ending with a vote on a class mascot. The capybara wins with 11 of 27 votes, ahead of the goose at 9 and the sloth at 7. The teacher puts the result on the board that morning.
fields.tab_content_4:
Friday starts with the result of Monday's question

At 9 am every Monday, a funny random question goes to the team channel in Slack with a link to answer. This week asked which meeting phrase should be retired. By Friday, 31 people had voted, and Let's take this offline won with 17. The result posts back to the channel before the Friday meeting.

fields.howto_title: How to Write Funny Survey Questions
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write funny survey questions that land with your crowd and bring back answers you can use.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what the answers are for
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Aim jokes at things, never people
fields.howto_step_1_des: Before you write the first joke, pick the job the answers will do, such as sorting teams or opening a meeting. A question that feeds that job earns its place. One that only gets a laugh can go.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write for the people who will read it. An inside joke lands with a team of 12 and confuses a company of 900, and a reference the whole group shares beats a clever one only three people get.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Aim each joke at the situation, like the coffee machine or the Monday meeting, and never at a person in the room. Leave out questions about looks or money altogether.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Use multiple choice for anything you want to tally, and keep one open box for the best one-liners. Even small wording differences can change the answers people give. Read each joke option next to the plain ones before you send it.
fields.howto_step_5_des: The order in which questions are asked can change how people answer. Open with the funny question as a warm-up, and keep it away from any serious question it could color.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Describe the crowd and what the answers should do. Emergent builds the survey and its vote tally from that prompt, and you reword any question with another prompt.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it with two people, then share
fields.howto_step_7_des: Send the survey to two people first and read their answers before everyone gets the link. Then show the result to the whole group, since the reveal is the part people remember.

faq_plan.a: Fun survey questions are light questions asked for a laugh or a warm-up, not for hard data, such as which office appliance you would be. Funny survey questions push the joke further. Give their answers a use, like a vote that names a team, and the laugh leads somewhere.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up funny survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Tell Emergent's AI survey builder who will answer and what the votes should decide. It builds the survey and the tally, with each response stored in your own database. Reword any question with a follow-up prompt, then share the link.

faq_plan.q: What are some funny survey questions?
faq_plan.ref: what are some funny survey questions
faq_plan.a: Here are six funny survey questions to ask, some for work and some for students. If the office were a sitcom, who would be the main character? Which snack would you guard with your life? What would your autobiography be called? Which animal should be the class mascot? Which emoji do you overuse? What is the worst phrase to hear in a meeting?

faq_plan.q: What are interesting survey questions to ask a team?
faq_plan.a: Interesting survey questions ask about something people have an opinion on but are rarely asked, such as the best advice they ever ignored or the skill they would learn with a month off. Keep questions about pay and workload for an employee satisfaction survey, where the answers are read as feedback.

faq_plan.q: What are funny survey questions and answers for a group?
faq_plan.a: Here are two, with answer choices that are funny on their own. Which office sound annoys you most: the microwave beep, the squeaky chair, the mystery alarm, or the keyboard that sounds like hail? What would your desk say about you: organized chaos, send snacks, I live here now, or please water the plant?

faq_plan.q: What are good funny family survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Good funny family survey questions let relatives vote on each other in a friendly way: who takes longest to get ready, who tells the same story every holiday, and who is most likely to bring three desserts. Keep every award one the winner would laugh at. With no response cap in Emergent, the whole extended family can vote on one link.

faq_plan.q: Where do funny random survey questions fit in an event?
faq_plan.a: Funny random survey questions fit best at the start of a post event survey, before anyone rates a session. A question like which session snack deserves an award of its own gets people answering, and the serious questions come after it.

faq_plan.q: What are safe funny survey questions for coworkers?
faq_plan.a: Safe funny survey questions for coworkers poke fun at shared things, never at people: the printer, the fridge, the meeting that should have been an email. Two to try: Which office supply would you take to a desert island? What phrase do you say most on calls?

faq_plan.q: How do you write funny multiple choice survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Write a plain question and let the answer choices carry the joke, with one sensible option so nobody feels pushed. Which meeting could have been an email: all of them, the Monday one, the one about meetings, or none, I love meetings? Emergent can run the survey one question per screen, and each set of choices gets read on its own.

faq_plan.q: Where do funny survey questions for employees go in a longer survey?
faq_plan.a: Put funny survey questions for employees at the start of a longer survey as a warm-up, outside the scored section. The same goes for a customer experience survey: one light opener, aimed at the product and never at the customer. Emergent builds that order from your prompt, and one more prompt moves the warm-up anywhere else.

plan.angle: The top 10 is lists of fun poll and survey questions (polly.ai, Formbricks, heysurvey, forms.app, Wooclap, SurveySparrow) plus Pinterest and Reddit threads. None of them says what the answers are for once they come back. This page gives the question lists in the FAQ (examples, answers, family, coworkers, multiple choice, students) and then shows four surveys where a funny question does a job: sorting an offsite into mixed teams, voting family awards for a reunion, picking a class mascot, and a weekly Slack question whose result opens the Friday meeting.

intent.evidence: Title promises examples and delivers them: FAQ 3 six questions, FAQ 5 two with answer choices, FAQ 6 family, FAQ 8 coworkers, FAQ 9 multiple choice; how-to on writing them.

truth.evidence: The page contradicts itself on where the funny question goes: howto_step_5_title 'Put the funny question first' vs faq item 7 'Funny random survey questions fit best at the end of a post event survey, after the ratings are in.' Emergent claims map to claims_used; the two survey-method facts in steps 4 and 5 match their Pew quoted spans.

distinct.evidence: Stories (offsite team sort, reunion awards, class mascot, weekly Slack question) are distinct from poll-questions; no sibling primary in a heading.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, each answered in its first sentence, secondaries read naturally; hub link in item 2.

images.evidence: Images match copy: 5 teams of 8, max 2 per department, Team Toaster 4 departments, 40 of 40; Dana 9 of 23; capybara 11, goose 9, sloth 7 of 27; offline 17 of 31 (17+8+4+2).
